title: TF1766 ↔ 1.766 Hz physical resonance
description: Testable hypothesis that the TF1766 reference used in the Spiral Flow framework corresponds to a physically observable 1.766 Hz resonance or dynamically privileged frequency.
definitions: A physical resonance claim requires an identifiable system, observable, coupling mechanism and reproducible measurement.
assumptions: 1.766 Hz is a candidate frequency to test, not an established universal constant.
The inverse-frequency time relation is a model layer and does not itself establish a physical resonance.
mechanism: Search measured spectra and dynamical systems for a reproducible, system-specific peak or invariant role at 1.766 Hz, while controlling for harmonics, aliases, sampling artifacts, environmental forcing and selection effects.
predictions: Independent datasets selected before analysis should contain a reproducible feature at 1.766 Hz or a predeclared tolerance band when the proposed mechanism predicts it.
The feature should have a measurable relation to the relevant system dynamics rather than being a numerical coincidence.
falsification_conditions: Predeclared independent datasets fail to reproduce the candidate feature after correction for resolution and known confounders.
The apparent feature is fully explained by an alias, harmonic, instrument artifact, environmental forcing or selection procedure.

evidence.source: UPI model calculation from f = 1.766 Hz
evidence.notes: Verifies arithmetic for the declared model input; does not verify physical resonance.

confusion_guard: Numerical relation to TF1766 is not evidence that nature contains a universal 1.766 Hz resonance.
